rows: 2025 Form 1120 · fiscal year July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026 (FY2026) · USD · EIN XX-XXX7890 (masked)
DRAFT · NOT FOR FILING · human review required; an officer signs and a person files

EQ-4410 hydraulic excavator, 30-ton class, $419,900.00: the purchase contract was signed December 2, 2024 and the excavator was placed in service August 14, 2025. Property acquired before January 20, 2025 gets the 40% allowance, so the draft deducts $218,348.00; the depreciation software took 100%, $419,900.00, $201,552.00 more. A person confirms the contract was binding on that date and corrects the register before Form 4562 is filed.

The board resolution approving FY2026 officer pay ($705,000.00: the President and CEO's and the Chief Financial Officer's salaries) was prepared July 8, 2025 and neither director has signed it. The draft deducts the salaries paid on line 12 and Form 1125-E; Riley Tanaka, Vice President and 40% shareholder, is listed with no pay. A person obtains the signed resolution.

Account 1210 holds $277,875.00 billed June 30, 2026 to Juniper Ridge Partners LLC, owned by the Vice President, a 40% shareholder, for job J-2625 under a cost-plus contract; it was paid July 20, 2026. A person confirms the contract's markup is what HANGS charges unrelated owners: a below-market price would move income to the Vice President's company and could be a constructive dividend.

No FY2026 estimated payment was made. FY2025 showed no tax, so the prior-year exception is not available, and HANGS is a large corporation (FY2024 taxable income $1,182,400.00). The regular method gives $511.21, entered on line 34. A person decides whether the annualized income installment method (Form 2220 Schedule A) lowers it, and whether to attach Form 2220.

The FY2026 books carry no income tax account: net income per books, $1,125,090.40, is before federal income tax, and Schedule M-1 line 2 is zero. The $12,650.79 of tax and the $511.21 penalty belong in the company's records; the controller records them with the Form 7004 payment.

Unsigned draft. The return was due September 15, 2026 (a June 30 year end files by the 15th day of the 3rd month); Form 7004, filed that day with $15,000.00, extends the time to file to April 15, 2027. The $1,838.00 overpayment is credited to FY2027 estimated tax; $2,663,212.52 of the loss carries to FY2027. Resolve the open items first; an officer signs and a person files. Nothing has been filed.
